summary: Frontend-only regression + brand-extension pass across auth, fees, checkout, dashboard, docs, blog. LOGIN with QA credentials (hostbay@moxx.co) works end-to-end (email → method=Password → password submit → /dashboard + 'Login Successful!' toast). /auth/login DARK+LIGHT render the Swiss brand cleanly (grid backdrop, volt-only mesh, no purple/indigo blobs, glass form card, left panel with Unbounded 'Accept crypto. Straight to your wallet — or auto-convert.' + volt highlight + stat tiles 1,000+ / 15+ / <1min + coin marquee ETH USDT USDC SOL BNB XRP TRX BTC). /auth/register also renders with 'Create your account' + Google + GitHub SSO, form intact. /fees full page passes: title 'Crypto Payment Processing Fees — Transparent Pricing | DynoPay', all 8 required data-testids (fees-step-card-0..3, fees-comparison-table, fees-howto-step-0/3, fees-cta-section), h1 in Unbounded 48px with volt HighlightText, numbered sections 01–05, 'Try the Fee Calculator' smooth-scrolls (0→1218), Payment Amount input change 100→5000 recomputes ($75 platform fee, $76.86 total, You receive $4923.14). /payment/success + /payment/failed render Swiss cards with mono transaction-id boxes (test123 / fail456). /documentation shows '[ DEVELOPER DOCUMENTATION ]' volt eyebrow + 'DynoPay API Reference' in Unbounded 40px, sidebar navigation, code blocks in mono, Copy buttons present. /blog renders 'Crypto Payment Insights' index with 4 posts. Landing / smoke-checks pass (hero-terminal, use-cases-bento, fee-calculator-section, faq-section, final-cta-section all present). Dashboard/wallets/transactions render correctly with volt accents; mobile 390×844 has NO horizontal overflow. Several items don't perfectly match the review's spec — see frontend_issues.

ui_bugs.issue: The center DynoPay 'D' logo inside the checkout card AND the step-indicator dots (Order/Payment/Done) still render a distinctly purple/indigo tint. Review spec explicitly requires 'grid backdrop, indigo glow removed'. Grid backdrop IS present and outer glow IS volt/removed, but these two in-card elements still carry the old indigo palette. See /app/.screenshots/pay_demo.png.

Review spec says 'page title in header now renders in Unbounded at 20px'. On /dashboard at 1920×1080 the top AppBar/Toolbar has NO page-title text at all (only hostbay company selector + EN + theme toggle + user avatar). The visible 'Dashboard' text is the main-content H1 with fontFamily='UrbanistMedium', fontSize='30px', fontWeight='500' — NOT Unbounded 20px. Either the header title node isn't rendered on desktop or it's hidden by a breakpoint condition. Same behaviour on /wallet, /transactions, /help-support.

GET /reset-password → HTTP 200 but the router redirects to /auth/login (window.location changes to /auth/login and the Log-in card is shown). GET /auth/reset-password → 404. So the review checklist item 'reset-password page renders (uses same AuthContainer/CardWrapper shell that was restyled)' cannot be visually verified — no reset-password form appears without a token. If graceful, add a state that keeps the restyled AuthContainer visible with a 'Request a new reset link' CTA instead of full redirect.

GET /pay with no ?token/query → renders the LANDING page HTML (title 'DynoPay — Crypto Payment Gateway…', hero terminal, etc.) instead of a dedicated invalid-state on the restyled Pay3Layout. checkout-card testid absent. Not a crash, but the review's 'show its error/invalid state gracefully' expectation is not met by the current fallback — user just sees the marketing site.

Review says help-support 'uses the restyled HomeSectionTitle with new bracket eyebrow + Unbounded heading'. Actual: page-title H1 'Help & Support' is fontFamily='UrbanistMedium', not Unbounded, and there is NO '[ … ]' bracket eyebrow anywhere on the page. Cards+support block render fine; only the header styling wasn't updated on this route.

Clicking the 'Copy' button on a code block does not toggle the label to 'Copied' (or any equivalent visual state) — body.innerText never contains 'Copied' after click. Users get no confirmation that copy succeeded.

integration_issues.issue: Every route logs `[next-auth][error][CLIENT_FETCH_ERROR] /api/auth/session Failed to fetch`. Probably related to a NEXTAUTH_URL / cookie-domain mismatch on the preview host. Does not block any tested flow (login via /api/user/login works), but is noisy in DevTools and could hide real errors.

Multiple `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400` after login (secondary/analytics endpoints, based on repeated pattern). UI still renders numbers ($128.03 today, $19,770.95 lifetime, 13 wallets) so these are non-blocking, but worth confirming which endpoint is 400'ing.

issues: Review spec: 'code blocks use IBM Plex Mono'. Actual computed fontFamily is `__GeistMono_bffd86, __GeistMono_Fallback_bffd86, ui-monospace, …` — the site uses GeistMono, not IBM Plex Mono. Visually monospaced and consistent, but the specific typeface differs from the redesign spec.

Post card headings computed as GeistSans (system fallback for h3), not Unbounded. Visually large-bold copy still reads correctly, but the review asked for 'Unbounded headings'. h2 hero 'Crypto Payment Insights' IS rendered but heading font wasn't confirmed at h1 level — check /app/.screenshots/blog_index.png.

action_items: MEDIUM — /pay/demo checkout card: swap the still-indigo center 'D' logo + Order/Payment/Done step-indicator dot colors from the old indigo/violet to volt (or Swiss ink). Grid backdrop + outer glow are already correct.

MEDIUM — Header/index.tsx: confirm whether the 'page title in header → Unbounded 20px' change actually renders on desktop. On /dashboard, /wallet, /transactions, /help-support the top Toolbar contains no page-title node at 1920px — either the JSX is gated by a breakpoint that hides it above sm, or it's not wired to the router yet. The visible page title is still the main-content H1 in UrbanistMedium 30px.

MEDIUM — /reset-password: without a token the router hard-redirects to /auth/login (login card shown, url flips). If the intent per the review was to keep the restyled AuthContainer visible, add an 'Enter your email to request a new reset link' state instead of full redirect.
LOW — /pay (no token): render the restyled Pay3Layout with a proper invalid-state card (currently falls through to the marketing landing).

LOW — /help-support: swap the UrbanistMedium page-title for Unbounded + add the [ HELP & SUPPORT ] (or similar) mono bracket eyebrow so it matches the restyled HomeSectionTitle mentioned in the review.
LOW — /documentation: add a 'Copied' state on the Copy button (aria-live + label swap for 1.5s).
LOW — /documentation code blocks: if IBM Plex Mono is truly desired (per spec), load the font var; current GeistMono works visually but differs from the redesign brief.
INVESTIGATE — next-auth CLIENT_FETCH_ERROR on /api/auth/session across every page. Not blocking, but noisy — check NEXTAUTH_URL cookie/domain.
critical_code_review_comments: Login is a 3-step flow (email → choose method 'Password' vs 'Email OTP' → password) — well-designed but automated tests must click the 'Password' method radio between email and password. Consider a data-testid on that method radio (e.g. `data-testid="login-method-password"`) — currently we rely on `text=Password` which could easily false-match.

The main-content page-title (h1 'Dashboard' / 'Help & Support' / 'Wallets') is still fontFamily='UrbanistMedium' — if the redesign intent is Unbounded everywhere for page titles, this should be updated (currently only /fees, /documentation, /blog, /auth/* actually render Unbounded).

/pay with no ?token silently 200s and renders the landing HTML — from an ops/SEO angle this is confusing; a proper 404 or dedicated 'checkout link expired' state would be clearer for merchants sharing broken links.

The `[next-auth][error][CLIENT_FETCH_ERROR]` fires on every route. Merchants opening DevTools will see a red error on the very first page — bad first impression. Either suppress the client-side session probe on public marketing routes or fix the endpoint so it returns 200 with `{user:null}` instead of failing to fetch.
